profile.constituencyprofile_Text: Madakasira (SC) Constituency comprising of 5 mandals Madakasira, Rolla, Agali, Gudibanda and Amarapuram mandals and Madakasira Nagar Panchayat in Sri Sathya Sai District in Andhra Pradesh that elects representatives to the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly . It is one of the seven assembly segments of Hindupur Lok Sabha constituency.592 Kms away from the State capital Amaravathi. Madakasira is a rain shadow zone with no industrial development for the past few decades. Industrial development would help and prevent large-scale migrations from the regions to Bangalore and other cities by youth and even skilled labourers. The Constituency is strategically located, connected major urban centers like Bangalore at just 105kms away, and Hindupur Town 32kms away. Spanning an area of 1082.87 Sq.km. Madakasira Constituency is significant potential in agriculture, horticulture and Sericulture, and eco-tourism. Besides the Madakasira Fort, there are many historical places in and around Madakasira, including Shiva temples and inscriptions. The hill on which the fort is located has a temple built during the Vijayanagara rule. The town has recently constructed a large Shirdi Sai Baba Temple. Sri Neelakanteswara swamy temple dedicated to Neelakantaswara Swamy recently constructed Ex. Minister G.Raghuveera Reddy which is located at Neelakantapuram village of Madakasira Mandal. There is Lord Shiva shines in the form of 5.8 feet Siddheswara in a quadrangular shape at Hemavathi village of Amarapuram Mandal. This temple was built in 9-10th century. The Doddeswara in Linga Shape temple here is very important for its sculpture. Pelubanda Ranganatha Swamy Temple located at Sivaram Village is famous temple. 10 Acres of land assigned in Halukuru village of Amarapuram mandal for installation of Arecanut processing unit. (C.M Assurances during the visit to Gundumala in August 2024) Vrushabbhanath Therthankarlu otherwise called as First Adinatha theerthankarlu Jain Temple located at Agali mandal headquarters . This temple was built also in 9-10th century. Belongs to IKSHWAKA PERIOD of Dasaratha and Sriramachandra. Ratnagiri Fort is a hill fort located in the Ratnagiri village in Rolla mandal located near the border of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka in the Rayalaseema region. It is also known as Seema Golconda ("Golconda at the border"). The Government of India has designated it as a Monument of National Importance. The fort spans over two hills, known as Ratnagiri and Venkatagiri. It has several structures, including the ruined Pattrappa temple. There is a large stepwell (kalyani), which was built as a swimming pool for a queen. The former bath area of the queen also has a Krishna shrine, where the queen performed puja (worship) after the bath. Another stepwell named Pala Bavi is used by the devotees visiting a temple dedicated to the goddess Kolhapuramma. An old Jain temple is located nearby. This diverse and resource-rich constituency is poised for balanced and sustainable development through targeted interventions. Pavagada is also famous for the Shani Mahatma Temple of god Shani. A special puja is performed at Pavagada at 5 a.m in Sravana masa (July-August) is good time to visit this temple where a huge crowd from different parts of the south india will assemble. This whole month will be celebrated in the name of god Shani which is situated in Karnataka, 20km away from Madakasira. Madakasira has a rich historical and administrative legacy. Established as a Municipal Nagar Panchayat in 2011 the region witnessed a transformative milestone in 2011 with the merger of Madakasira and Mallinayakahalli Villages.
profile.geography: Madakasira (SC) Assembly Constituency is strategically located in Sri Satya Sai District within and near to  Karnataka Capital Bangalore Region, benefiting from its proximity to Sira, Madhugiri and  chitradurga towns of Karnataka. The region has a mix of Red soil (74%) and red loamy soil (26%), supporting a variety of crops. The constituency is situated in a semi-arid region with a relatively flat terrain It is part of the Deccan Plateau, characterized by rocky outcrops and dryland agriculture. Madakasira’s geography is characterized by area of rain shadow zone with red and sandy soils. A network of MI Tanks, including the Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi project is the longest water canal project in the region of Rayalaseema. The project was conceived to provide a reliable irrigation and drinking water supply for the region through drawing flood waters from the Srisailam reservoir canal, which is life line for irrigation and drinking water supply.

•		Total Population: 2,65,825 in 59,149 Households.
•	Male Population: 1,34,890 and Female Population: 1,30,935
•	Children Under 6-years of age: 27,381
The sex ratio is 970 female per 1000 males. The constituency boats a the literacy rate is 61.77 %, 70.77 % of the male population and 52.5 % of the female population are literate.

Madakasira (SC) is a major agricultural educational hub ( N G Ranga Agricultural University along with Agricultural Polytechnic). School education is being strengthened with 350 schools, 100+ smart classrooms.
The healthcare sector includes 9 PHCs, 66 sub-centers, 1 CHCs, and 3 AYUSH dispensaries, with plans to reduce maternal mortality by 50%, bring infant mortality below 10 per 1,000 live births, and achieve 100% vaccination.

economy_text.economy_Text:
The economy of Madakasira is poised for robust growth, with its Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) projected to increase from Rs 5,467 crores in 2023-24 to Rs 11,499 crores by 2028-29, driven by a consistent annual growth rate of 16.12%. 

The agricultural sector, led by horticulture and livestock, remains the economic backbone, supported by precision farming, high-value crops, and climate resilience measures. 

The industry sector is transforming through infrastructure investments and emerging industries like granite and defense manufacturing, with GVA rising from Rs 690 crores to Rs 1,613 crores. 

The service sector, a key growth engine, is expected to grow from Rs 1,284 crores to Rs 2,667 crores, fueled by urban expansion, IT, hospitality, and digital services. 

Strategic thrust areas include MSME cluster development, tourism infrastructure, and smart governance, aligning with the Swarna Andhra @ 2047 vision for diversified and inclusive economic progress.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Madakasira is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like real estate, infrastructure and agriculture. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant urban and economic hub by 2047
